title: ERIS vs Notion
content_html:
ERIS and Notion are both AI workspaces, but they are built for different problems. Notion excels at flexible knowledge management, documentation and team collaboration in a single visual workspace. ERIS is built as a complete business system that replaces multiple tools (CRM, finance, projects, documents, meetings, chat) with one platform and local AI that runs on your own servers.

Pick Notion if your team needs a flexible, visual workspace for capturing knowledge, managing documents and collaborating across departments. Pick ERIS if your company runs separate business tools today and wants to replace them with one system where AI works across all your data without sending it to outside providers.

What Notion is good at

According to its website, Notion is an AI workspace for teams to capture context, find answers and automate tasks. It describes itself as a workspace where teams get more done by building custom agents, searching across all apps and automating busywork.

Notion offers offline use on desktop and mobile apps. For Enterprise plan workspaces, its LLM providers use zero data retention when Notion AI is used, according to its website. The Plus plan connects to tools like Slack and Google Drive. The Business plan connects to GitHub, Asana and more. The Enterprise plan connects to SIEM and DLP tools to automatically centralize audit logs.

Notion's strength is flexibility. It works as a blank canvas for teams to build their own structure for notes, databases, wikis and workflows. It is designed for knowledge work where the shape of the information is not fixed in advance.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS is built as a complete business system, not a flexible workspace. It comes with modules for specific business functions: CRM, project management, document management with e-signature, meetings with AI note-taking, team chat, bookkeeping, tax returns, procurement and more. All modules run on the same data layer with one login and one audit trail.

ERIS is built to run on your company's own servers with local AI models. This means the AI that answers questions from your business data does not send that data to outside AI providers. With the on-premise option, the data stays inside your building. ERIS can also be hosted by Upward Technologies on its own servers in the Netherlands for companies without their own hardware, and it still uses local AI models.

Every question asked to the ERIS Assistant is logged: who asked, which data was used, what the AI did and the result. The assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. A refused access is logged like every other question.

ERIS is in development. The beta starts in November 2026 with design partners, and the official release is in January 2027. Read more about how local AI works and what it requires.

Which one should you pick

Pick Notion if:

  • Your team is primarily doing knowledge work: writing, research, documentation, wikis or flexible note-taking.
  • You need a blank canvas to design your own workflows and information structure.
  • You want integrations with many external tools and apps.
  • You are comfortable with AI answers that may use your data for model improvement (zero data retention is only on Enterprise).

Pick ERIS if:

  • Your company runs many separate business tools today (a CRM, a finance tool, a project tracker, a chat app, a document manager) and you want to replace them with one system.
  • You need AI to work across all your business data in one place, not inside a single tool.
  • Your data cannot or should not leave your company's servers (for compliance, security, or policy reasons).
  • You want one login, one price per user and one audit trail across all your business functions.
  • You have the hardware to run ERIS on your own servers, or you prefer a hosted option in the Netherlands with local AI models.

Neither is the right choice if:

  • You need a solution that is available today. ERIS is in development and will release in January 2027.
  • You need only one or two business functions (for example, a CRM or a project tracker alone). Notion and ERIS are both multi-function platforms.
  • You need deep integrations with industry-specific software. Check the integrations both platforms offer for your specific tools.

FAQ

Can I use Notion for my entire business?

Notion can be used for documentation, knowledge management and some project tracking. It is not built as a complete business system with CRM, accounting, tax returns or other business functions that ERIS includes. If your company needs a single platform for sales, finance, operations and knowledge work, Notion is not designed for that.

Does ERIS work offline?

ERIS is designed to run on your company's own servers or in the Upward cloud. Offline use is not a focus of the product. If your team needs offline access on mobile or desktop, Notion is the better choice.

Can I connect ERIS to my existing tools?

Custom modules, agents and knowledge bases are built for a company as projects and billed separately. Upward Technologies also builds ERP and CRM integrations. ERIS is not designed to be a hub that connects many external tools the way Notion is. It is built to replace separate tools with one system.

How much does each cost?

Notion offers free and premium plans. Pricing details are on its website. ERIS pricing depends on company size and the number of users. For details, see the ERIS pricing page.

Is my data safe with ERIS?

ERIS is built with local AI models that run on your own servers or in the Upward cloud in the Netherlands. Data does not go to outside AI providers. Every AI question and action is logged. Whether a specific deployment meets your compliance requirements depends on your use case and is assessed per deployment. Read more about how on-premises AI keeps data inside the firewall.
